content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Erika Bolton (E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes:
- Note 1 says full_time Analyst, recommend write.
- Note 2 says contractor with basic security training, recommend read.

The notes disagree on employment type. Note 2 says Security DB shows contractor and bases recommendation on Security DB.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns). So max write.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read.

Either way, admin is above the maximum. Since requested level (admin) is above maximum, grant the maximum.

Which maximum applies? If full-time → write. If contractor with basic → read. The conflict: Note 2 says Security DB shows contractor, basing on that. As the Approver, I need to decide. There's a discrepancy. The Security DB note appears more authoritative (it explicitly flags the earlier note as incorrect). But the team memory shows conflict.

Hmm. The question is what evidence to use. Note 2 from Security says contractor with basic security training. So max is read. Requested admin > read, grant read.

If we take the full-time note, max is write, grant write (since admin > write, grant maximum write, not more than requested—admin requested, grant write which is below requested? Wait, "Never grant more than the requested level." Requested is admin. Granting write is less than admin, so fine. Granting admin is not allowed).

So the decision depends on employment type. Which note is reliable? The security DB note says it's basing on Security DB. This seems to be the more updated/authoritative source. Also two notes disagree; the second note explicitly addresses the conflict.

I'll go with contractor/basic → max read → grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
